resources.string: Off by default. When enabled, your saved system prompt, fixed input/output instructions, transcript chunks and personal vocabulary are sent as text to this configured server; audio is never sent. 127.0.0.1 refers to this phone. Polishing requires support for JSON-schema responses; on failure the original transcript is kept.

Enter the server base URL and model. For example, http://127.0.0.1:11434 with model default. The app calls /v1/chat/completions (or /chat/completions when the URL ends in /v1). HTTP is restricted to this phone; use HTTPS for other hosts.
Configuration saved. Test the connection before enabling.
Connection successful. The model returned OK.

Edit the polishing instructions and save to apply them. Fixed input/output instructions are appended when sending your prompt, transcript chunks and custom vocabulary to the server. The connection test uses synthetic text and does not check the prompt or JSON-schema support. Maximum 12,000 characters. Restore the built-in prompt at any time.
Choose 2–4 threads for Nemotron recognition. Changes apply to subsequent recognition sessions. Speed, battery use and heat depend on your device.
Processes audio during recording. Multilingual, with automatic language detection. INT8; ~475 MB download. Chunk size is not end-to-end latency.

Recent ML Kit diagnostic events are kept automatically in memory (up to 40), and disappear when the app process ends. The report includes the app version, status, phase, known exception class, recognized fixed SDK error type or generic reason, and optional numeric codes; it does not record device metadata, audio, transcripts, exception messages, or endpoints. Copy places the report on the system clipboard, where it may be exposed to apps or wherever you paste it.
Remove the in-memory ML Kit diagnostic events?
ML Kit diagnostics copied to clipboard
Show a movable, two-line live preview while dictating with the floating button. Preview text may be visible to others and can differ from the final transcript. Changes apply to the next recording.
Live preview is not available for the selected model in this app.
Required to detect focused text fields and insert dictation
Required to show the floating dictation button
50–150% of the original size. Changes apply immediately. Drag partly beyond any screen edge; a small part stays reachable.
Temporarily hide the floating button when an autofill popup or another app/system window is over the focused text field.

Useful when an app does not expose text-field focus. Overrides collision hiding and can show over password or banking screens. Android may still block overlays in apps that explicitly hide them; dictation may then copy to the clipboard if the field is inaccessible.

Start, leave the app to reproduce the issue, then return to inspect the timeline. Recording stops after 10 minutes and holds up to 500 entries. Data is in memory only and is lost if the app process dies. App package names may be sensitive and may be unavailable due to Android restrictions; field text and transcripts are not recorded. Copying places the report on the system clipboard, exposing it to apps or wherever you paste it. Android may physically hide the overlay even when the app reports it visible.

Starting replaces the previous report. Recording stops after 10 minutes; the report stays in memory until cleared, replaced, or the app process ends. Copying exposes the report on the system clipboard and wherever it is pasted.\n\nOptional names come from accessibility or input providers when Android cannot verify them. They are marked unverified and limited to ASCII package-like syntax, but may reveal sensitive information and may not identify a real app. Even a name-shaped string could contain sensitive data. Field text, hints, selections, and transcripts are not collected.
Include unverified provider-supplied package names for this recording
Clear the in-memory diagnostics report? Recording continues if it is active.

Post-transcript spelling only: recases or joins/splits spaces when the recognized letters already match. Independent of the experimental acoustic hotword switch in the Vocabulary tab; these hints cannot correct sound-alike recognition.

Nemotron only; ML Kit Advanced does not use acoustic word boosting. Off by default. Word boosting uses modified beam search and can change, repeat or omit speech; accuracy is not guaranteed. Only plain text terms (letters, digits, spaces, apostrophes or hyphens) are used for acoustic bias; unsupported saved entries remain available as spelling hints.

Enabled by default for um, uhm and uh. Edit one word or phrase per line, then Save. Matches whole words without case sensitivity, never parts of real words. Only final text changes, across floating, live and file dictation. Clear the list or switch off to keep everything. Settings are read when transcription begins.
Words or phrases to remove (one per line)
Use up to 100 entries, each up to 80 characters: letters, numbers, spaces, apostrophes or hyphens. No regular expressions.

Add names or technical terms here. They can be used as post-transcript spelling hints and, when enabled below, as experimental acoustic word boosts. Boosting can repeat terms or alter unrelated speech; it is off by default and is not accuracy-guaranteed.
No custom terms yet. Add terms above to use as spelling hints or experimental acoustic word boosts.
Convert clear English number phrases to digits
Converts clear number phrases and decimals, such as “twenty one” and “two point five”. A standalone “one” stays spelled out.

Below the minimum only: polish when “one” appears as a whole word (except “one another”), or when two or more number tokens are within two intervening words, such as “4 30 pm”. Requires the master AI-polishing switch. AI uses context to decide whether “one” means 1; static conversion leaves standalone “one” unchanged.

Map common transcription variants to the intended text. Each rule can have several input alternatives, one per line. Matching is case-insensitive and respects whole words and phrases; replacements apply to final transcripts.
No custom replacements yet. Add a rule to map common transcription variants to the text you want.
One literal phrase per line; up to 20 alternatives per rule.
Enter 1–20 non-empty alternatives, each no longer than 120 characters.
Enter replacement text up to 120 characters.
An input already belongs to another rule. Each input can map to only one output.
Up to 50 rules and 200 input alternatives total are supported.
Remove all %1$d custom string replacement rules?

Android backup can save settings and transcript history if enabled on your device. Downloaded models and audio are excluded from cloud backup. Export settings, vocabulary, replacement rules and polishing configuration to an unencrypted JSON file; it may contain private information. JSON excludes history, audio, downloaded models and system permissions.

Import replaces your current settings and reopens the app. Unsaved settings edits will be discarded, and an active dictation may stop if the imported settings disable the service. History and recordings will be kept.
Could not import settings. Check the file; if storage failed, some settings may have changed.

Original audio is stored privately on this device, excluded from backups, and removed when its history entry is deleted or trimmed. Reprocessing replaces the transcript only. Older entries have no saved audio.
Cannot reprocess: audio, model, or service unavailable.
Reprocessing failed; the existing transcript was kept.

This will decode the saved recording again on-device with your currently selected model and replace this History transcript. No text or audio is sent to a server. The original audio is kept. Continue?

This will decode the saved recording again and replace this History transcript; the original audio is kept. AI polishing is enabled. If you continue, the configured system prompt, fixed input/output instructions, resulting transcript chunks, and your personal vocabulary (%3$d terms) will be sent as text to %1$s using model %2$s. Audio stays on this device. This retry will not be redirected if server settings change.
Could not play the saved audio.
No transcriptions recorded yet. Focus any text field across the system and tap the floating dictation button.
Voice Dictation Accessibility Service detects when text input fields are focused to display the floating dictation button and directly injects recognized speech into the active text field.
